title: What we need to know
description: Every open question about this industry, grouped by domain, with what we already hold and what would close it. Status is answered, partial or open. This is the research agenda.

questions.question: How many merchant ships are there?
questions.what_we_know: 112,501 at 100 GT and above, 2.44bn DWT, UNCTAD 1 Jan 2025.
questions.why_it_matters: Denominator for everything.

questions.question: How many ships of each type, by COUNT not tonnage?
questions.what_we_know: UNCTAD publishes the split by DWT only. We cannot say how many bulk carriers exist.
questions.how_to_answer: Clarksons, Equasis annual report, or IHS.
questions.why_it_matters: Sizes the addressable fleet in hulls, which is how escort is sold.

questions.question: How many containers move per year?
questions.what_we_know: 920m TEU port throughput 2024. Port moves double-count transhipment, so this is not unique containers.
questions.how_to_answer: UNCTAD plus a transhipment share figure.
questions.why_it_matters: Direct answer to how much cargo is at risk.

questions.question: What is the average container ship size?
questions.what_we_know: 30.3m TEU total cellular capacity, April 2025. No ship count, so no average.
questions.how_to_answer: Divide capacity by ship count once we have the count.
questions.why_it_matters: Tells us how much value sits on one hull.

questions.question: How much does each container pay?
questions.what_we_know: FBX global composite $3,532 per FEU on 2026-09-04; Asia-N Europe $4,641; Asia-USEC $9,791.
questions.why_it_matters: Revenue per hull, and the size of the cargo interest.

questions.question: What does it cost to run a ship for a day?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing. Bunkers only.
questions.how_to_answer: Moore OpCost, or listed owners' disclosed daily opex in quarterly reports.
questions.why_it_matters: Escort price only means something as a share of daily cost.

questions.question: What are charter rates?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing retrieved.
questions.how_to_answer: Baltic Exchange, Clarksons, or listed owner TCE disclosures.
questions.why_it_matters: The opportunity cost of a delayed or rerouted voyage.

questions.question: What does war risk cost?
questions.what_we_know: Full Reuters series 0.03% pre-campaign to over 1% in July 2026, quoted per seven-day cover.
questions.why_it_matters: The budget we compete with.

questions.question: What does maritime security cost today?
questions.what_we_know: Only 2012: $5,000 a day for a four-man team, up to $60,000 a transit.
questions.why_it_matters: Our entire price anchor is fourteen years old.

questions.question: What does an escort service cost?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing published by anyone, ever.
questions.how_to_answer: Convoy Escort Programme filings, or ask a provider.
questions.why_it_matters: There is no market price to anchor against.

questions.question: What does rerouting cost?
questions.what_we_know: +3,500 nm, +10 days, +40% fuel, about $1m a day for the largest boxships.
questions.why_it_matters: The real competitor is the Cape, not a rival vendor.

questions.question: What are P&I costs?
questions.what_we_know: General increases: Steamship 5% then 8%, NorthStandard 5%, Gard about 5%.
questions.why_it_matters: Shows the direction of the whole risk cost stack.

questions.question: How many attacks per year?
questions.what_we_know: IMB series 2010-2024: 445 down to 116. Plus 137 in 2025 and 38 in H1 2026.
questions.why_it_matters: The demand signal.

questions.question: How long is a ship exposed?
questions.what_we_know: Gulf of Aden IRTC is 490 nm, 33-49 hours depending on speed. No equivalent for Bab el-Mandeb.
questions.how_to_answer: Chart measurement plus a corridor definition.
questions.why_it_matters: This is the mission length. It defines the product.

questions.question: What is the attack probability per transit?
questions.what_we_know: About 0.55% per transit, Red Sea 2024. And only 40.4% of all recorded attacks happen to a ship under way, so the escort-addressable share is smaller again.
questions.how_to_answer: Divide incidents by transits per corridor once we have both.
questions.why_it_matters: If the per-voyage risk is tiny, no premium argument works.

questions.question: Are ships getting safer or more dangerous?
questions.what_we_know: Safer, and because of protection. Losses fell 79% and piracy 74% since 2010. NATO, IMB and the World Bank attribute the piracy fall to naval presence, corridors, hardening and armed guards.
questions.why_it_matters: Cuts against our own story and we should know it.

questions.question: Who actually decides?
questions.what_we_know: Inferred from ISM and ISPS: DPA, CSO, fleet director, charterer. Never confirmed with a practitioner.
questions.how_to_answer: Ask one DPA. We now know one.
questions.why_it_matters: The whole target list rests on this assumption.

questions.question: How is armed guarding procured today?
questions.what_we_know: Unknown. Through the manager, charterer, broker or direct?
questions.why_it_matters: The purchase path for the substitute is ours.

questions.question: Would an insurer discount for escort?
questions.what_we_know: No evidence either way.
questions.how_to_answer: Ask a war risk underwriter or P&I club.
questions.why_it_matters: If yes, the product sells on the insurance line.

questions.question: Has any commercial operator bought autonomous escort?
questions.what_we_know: No. A deliberate search found zero transactions.
questions.why_it_matters: We are creating the category, not entering it.

questions.question: Who are the charterers?
questions.what_we_know: One named: Cargill. They bear the premium on most charter types.
questions.why_it_matters: Structurally the best-motivated buyer.

questions.question: Who are the offshore energy operators?
questions.what_we_know: Zero catalogued. Six of ten incumbents serve them.
questions.why_it_matters: Second most-served buyer type, entirely missing.

questions.question: Who else builds this?
questions.what_we_know: 123 companies catalogued. Seasats at 4/4, BlackSea at 3/4.

questions.question: Who buys from the incumbents?
questions.what_we_know: Buyer types for ten providers. Only one hard-named end client, a government mission.
questions.why_it_matters: Nine of ten publish no client. The industry hides its customer list.

questions.question: What happened to the Convoy Escort Programme?
questions.what_we_know: Operated 2012, seven armoured patrol boats. Fate unknown.
questions.why_it_matters: The only precedent. Its failure mode is what repeats.

questions.question: Can an uncrewed vessel legally escort a crewed one?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing. Not researched at all.
questions.how_to_answer: IMO MASS Code work, flag state guidance, a maritime lawyer.
questions.why_it_matters: This may be the binding constraint, not price or technology.

questions.question: Who is the master of an uncrewed escort, and which COLREGs apply?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the product is deployable at all.

questions.question: Does BMP recognise escort?
questions.what_we_know: Not checked.
questions.why_it_matters: If escort is absent from BMP, a manager has no framework to justify it.

questions.question: What are the rules on armed uncrewed platforms in territorial waters?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines where we can operate.

domains.parked_note: Parked on 2026-09-04 at the founder's direction. The questions stay on the list because they do not stop being true; they are simply not the current priority.

questions.question: What can we actually commit to today?
questions.what_we_know: Unknown to me. The outreach says 'we can escort them', which nothing in this library supports.
questions.why_it_matters: Blocks every email in the sequence.

questions.question: What does our platform cost to build and operate per day?
questions.what_we_know: Nothing recorded.
questions.why_it_matters: Without it there is no margin model.

questions.question: Can our platform hold merchant speed for 33 to 49 hours?
questions.what_we_know: Not recorded. The corridor demands it.
questions.why_it_matters: This is the engineering requirement the route data implies.
